experiment_data.hypothesis: Extended analysis of existing action trajectory data: (1) temporal coherence — L1 ablation disrupts step-to-step action autocorrelation more than control, (2) bootstrap CI on per-head effect size — formal test of whether instruction heads per-head d (0.027) differs significantly from control heads per-head d (0.051).

bootstrap_per_head_d.interpretation: Control heads ~1.9x per-head effect; instruction heads achieve larger total via 24-head collective coordination

temporal_coherence_proxy.interpretation: Instruction ablation produces more consistent (low CV) and more task-dependent (high I²) perturbation, consistent with structured language-dependent computation

experiment_data.notes: Per-head effect formally confirmed: control heads ~1.9x stronger per-head (d=0.051 vs 0.027, p=0.0018). But instruction heads show qualitatively different perturbation: more consistent across dimensions (CV 1.30 vs 2.74) and more task-dependent (I²=0.87 vs 0.78). Instruction heads mediate structured, coordinated computation rather than individual strong effects.
